title.zh: 卷十三 本紀第十三: 衞紹王
title.raw: 卷十三 本紀第十三: 衞紹王 Volume 13 Annals 13: Wei Shaowang

sentences.zh: 衛紹王諱永濟，小字興勝，更諱允濟，章宗時避顯宗諱，詔改「允」為「永」。

translations.literal: Wei Shaowang, taboo name Yongji, childhood name Xingsheng, formerly taboo-named Yunji; during Zhangzong's reign, to avoid Xianzong's taboo, an edict changed "Yun" to "Yong."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shaowang—taboo name Yongji, childhood name Xingsheng, once taboo-named Yunji—during Zhangzong's reign, because of the taboo on Xianzong's name, received an edict changing yun to yong.

sentences.zh: 世宗第七子，母曰元妃李氏。

translations.literal: He was the seventh son of Shizong; his mother was Yuan Consort of the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was Shizong's seventh son; his mother was Yuan Consort Li.

sentences.zh: 衛王長身，美髯鬚，天資儉約，不好華飾，大定十一年，封薛王。

translations.literal: Prince Wei was tall, with a handsome beard; by nature he was frugal and disliked lavish adornment. In the eleventh year of Dading he was enfeoffed Prince of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei stood tall, with a fine beard; he was frugal by nature and shunned ornament. In Dading year 11 he was made Prince of Xue.

sentences.zh: 是歲，進封禭王。

translations.literal: That same year he was advanced to Prince of Cui.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was advanced to Prince of Cui.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授世襲猛安。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was granted a hereditary meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he received a hereditary meng'an commission.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，加開府義同三司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was given Grand Marshal with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he was made grand marshal with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，為秘書監。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he became Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he became director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉刑部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 又明年，改殿前都點檢。

translations.literal: The year after, he was made Chief Inspector of the Palatial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he became chief inspector of the palatial guards.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，世宗崩，章宗即位，進封潞王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Shizong died and Zhangzong ascended; he was advanced to Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 Shizong died and Zhangzong took the throne; he was advanced to Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 起複，判安武軍節度使。

translations.literal: He left mourning and was assigned as military governor of Anwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He left mourning and was posted as military governor of Anwu Army.

sentences.zh: 五月，至冀州，以到任表謝，賜詔優答。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he reached Jizhou, submitted a memorial of thanks on taking office, and received a gracious reply edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he reached Jizhou, thanked the throne for his appointment, and received a warm reply edict.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，進封韓王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang he was advanced to Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang year 2 he was advanced to Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 四年，改判興平軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was reassigned to Xingping Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was reassigned to Xingping Army.

sentences.zh: 五年，改沁南軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Qinnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was transferred to Qinnan Army.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，改封衛王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengan he was made Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengan year 2 he was made Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 三年，改昭義軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was assigned to Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was assigned to Zhaoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，改判彰德府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe he was put in charge of Zhangde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 1 he was put in charge of Zhangde Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，改判平陽府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was put in charge of Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was put in charge of Pingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，章宗誅鄭王永蹈、趙王永中，久，頗悔之。

translations.literal: Initially Zhangzong had executed Prince of Zheng Yongtao and Prince of Zhao Yongzhong; after a long while he deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhangzong had put Prince of Zheng Yongtao and Prince of Zhao Yongzhong to death; in time he came to regret it deeply.

sentences.zh: 七年，下詔追復舊封，仍賜諡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he issued an edict posthumously restoring their former titles and granting posthumous names.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he issued an edict restoring their former titles and bestowing posthumous names.

sentences.zh: 而永蹈無後，乃以衛王子按陳為鄭王後，賜衛王詔曰：「朕念鄭王自棄天常，以幹國憲，槁瘞曠野，忽諸不祀。

translations.literal: Yongtao had no heir, so the Prince of Wei's son An Chen was made successor to Prince of Zheng. An edict to Prince Wei said: "I reflect on Prince of Zheng, who abandoned Heaven's constants and violated state law, withered in burial on the open plain, gone suddenly without sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtao left no heir, so Prince Wei's son An Chen was made heir to Prince of Zheng. The edict to Prince Wei ran: "I think of Prince of Zheng, who threw away Heaven's law and breached the state's statutes, left to wither in the wild, and passed from sacrifice altogether.

sentences.zh: 歷歲既久，深用愴然。

translations.literal: Years have passed and I am deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Years have gone by, and grief weighs on me.

sentences.zh: 親親之情。

translations.literal: The bonds of kin weigh upon me.
translations.idiomatic: Kinship tugs at the heart.

sentences.zh: 有懷難置。

translations.literal: My heart cannot find rest.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot set the feeling aside.

sentences.zh: 已詔追復舊爵，改葬如儀。

translations.literal: I have already ordered his former title restored and burial redone according to rite.
translations.idiomatic: I have already ordered his old rank restored and a proper reburial.

sentences.zh: 稽考古禮，以卿之子按陳為鄭王後，謹其祭祀，卿其悉之。

translations.literal: Examining ancient rites, I make your son An Chen successor to Prince of Zheng to tend his sacrifices—see that you know this fully.
translations.idiomatic: By the ancient rites, your son An Chen is made heir to Prince of Zheng to keep his sacrifices—take full heed of this.

sentences.zh: 」已而改武定軍節度使。

translations.literal: " Thereafter he was reassigned as military governor of Wuding Army.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter he was posted as military governor of Wuding Army.

sentences.zh: 八年十一月，自武定軍入朝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year he entered court from Wuding Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 8 he came to court from Wuding Army.

sentences.zh: 是時，章宗已感嗽疾，衛王且辭行，而章宗意留之。

translations.literal: By then Zhangzong had contracted a coughing illness; Prince Wei was about to take leave, but Zhangzong intended to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhangzong had fallen ill with a cough; Prince Wei was ready to depart, but Zhangzong meant to keep him at court.

sentences.zh: 宗章初年，雅愛諸王，置王傳府尉官以傳導德義。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhangzong's reign he had dearly loved the princes and appointed tutors and household officers in each princely establishment to convey moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhangzong's reign he had loved his brothers dearly and set tutors and household officers in each prince's house to teach virtue.

sentences.zh: 及永中、永蹈之誅，由是疏忌宗室，遂以王傅府尉檢制王家，苛部嚴密，門戶出入皆有籍。

translations.literal: After the executions of Yongzhong and Yongtao, he grew distant and suspicious of the imperial clan, and used princes' tutors and household officers to control princely households—harshly regulated, with every entry and exit recorded.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongzhong and Yongtao were killed, he grew wary of the clan and turned the princes' tutors and household officers into overseers—rules were tight, and every coming and going at the gates was logged.

sentences.zh: 而衛王乃永蹈母弟，柔弱鮮智能，故章宗愛之。

translations.literal: Prince Wei was Yongtao's younger brother by the same mother—gentle, weak, and little gifted—so Zhangzong favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei was Yongtao's uterine younger brother—soft, ungifted, and mild—so Zhangzong held him dear.

sentences.zh: 既無繼嗣，而諸叔兄弟多在，章宗皆不肯立，惟欲立衛王，故於辭行留之。

translations.literal: With no heir of his own and many uncles and brothers still living, Zhangzong would establish none of them; he only wished to make Prince Wei his successor, and therefore detained him when he sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, and many uncles and brothers still lived; Zhangzong would raise none of them, wishing only to make Prince Wei heir—so when Prince Wei tried to leave, he was kept back.

sentences.zh: 無何，章宗大漸，元妃李氏、黃門李新喜、平章政事完顏匡定策。

translations.literal: Before long Zhangzong fell critically ill; Yuan Consort Li, Palace Attendant Li Xinxhi, and Grand Councilor Wanyan Kuang settled the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhangzong was near death; Yuan Consort Li, palace attendant Li Xinxhi, and Grand Councilor Wanyan Kuang fixed the succession.

sentences.zh: 章宗崩，匡等傳遣詔，立衛王。

translations.literal: Zhangzong died; Kuang and the others transmitted the death edict and enthroned Prince Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong died; Kuang and his party passed on the final edict and set Prince Wei on the throne.

sentences.zh: 衛王固讓，乃承詔舉哀，即皇帝位於柩前。

translations.literal: Prince Wei firmly declined, then accepted the edict and mourned, ascending the throne before the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei refused at first, then took the edict, raised the lament, and became emperor before the bier.

sentences.zh: 明日，群臣朝見于大安殿。

translations.literal: The next day the hundred officials paid homage in the Hall of Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the hundred officials attended him in the Hall of Great Peace.

sentences.zh: 詔路府州縣為大行皇帝服七日。

translations.literal: An edict ordered circuit, prefecture, and county offices to observe seven days' mourning for the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered every circuit, prefecture, and county to mourn the late emperor for seven days.

sentences.zh: 大安元年正月辛丑，飛星如火。

translations.literal: First year of Da'an, first month, xinchou: a shooting star like fire.
translations.idiomatic: Da'an year 1, first month, on xinchou, a shooting star blazed like fire.

sentences.zh: 起天市垣，有尾，跡若赤龍。

translations.literal: It rose from the Celestial Market wall, trailed, and its track resembled a red dragon.
translations.idiomatic: It rose from the Celestial Market Enclosure, left a tail, and its path looked like a red dragon.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，改元，大赦。

translations.literal: On renxu the era name was changed and a general amnesty proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the reign title was changed and a great amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 立元妃徒單氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Yuan Consort of the Tudan clan was made empress.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Consort of the Tudan clan was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 二月乙丑朔，太白晝見，經天。

translations.literal: Second month, yichou new moon: Venus appeared by day and crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the yichou new moon, Venus shone by day and crossed heaven.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，章宗內人范氏損其遣腹，以詔內外。

translations.literal: On renchen Zhangzong's inner attendant Fan harmed the pregnancy she was carrying for him; an edict announced this within and without.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Zhangzong's inner woman Fan injured the child she bore for him; an edict told the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 初，章宗遣詔：「內人有娠者兩人，生男則立為儲貳。

translations.literal: Initially Zhangzong had issued an edict: "Among inner women, two are pregnant; if a son is born he shall be made heir."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhangzong had sent an edict: "Two inner women are with child; whichever bears a son shall be made heir."

sentences.zh: 」至是平章政事僕散端等奏：「承御賈氏當以十一月免乳，今則已出三月。

translations.literal: " At this Grand Councilor Pusan Duan and others memorialized: "Palace Lady Jia should have ended nursing in the eleventh month; it is now three months past.
translations.idiomatic: " Then Grand Councilor Pusan Duan and others reported: "Palace Lady Jia should have weaned in the eleventh month; three months have passed since.

sentences.zh: 范氏產期合在正月，醫稱胎氣有損，用藥調治，脈息雖和，胎形已失。

translations.literal: Fan's due term should have been the first month. Physicians said the fetal qi was damaged; though pulse remained calm after medicine, the form of the fetus was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's term should have fallen in the first month. Physicians said the fetal breath was harmed; though her pulse stayed even under treatment, the fetus was already gone.

sentences.zh: 范氏願削髮為尼。

translations.literal: Fan wished to shave her head and become a nun."
translations.idiomatic: Fan asks to shave her head and take the tonsure."

sentences.zh: 」封皇子六人為王。

translations.literal: Six imperial sons were enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: Six imperial sons were made princes.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，道陵禮成，大赦。

translations.literal: Third month, on jiawu, Daoling rites were completed and a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu, rites at Daoling were completed and a great amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自今於朕名不連續，及昶、詠等字，不須別改。

translations.literal: An edict said: 「From now on my name need not be written with full taboo continuity, and characters such as Chang and Yong need not be specially altered.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 「From now my name need not be written with full taboo continuity, and characters such as chang and yong need not be specially changed.

sentences.zh: 」以平章政事僕散端為右丞相。

translations.literal: 」Participation Councillor Pusan Duan was made right chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: 」Participation Councillor Pusan Duan was appointed right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 四月庚辰，殺章宗元妃李氏及承御賈氏。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on gengwu, Zhangzong’s Primary Consort Li shi and Palace Woman Jia shi were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on gengwu, Zhangzong’s Primary Consort Li shi and Palace Woman Jia shi were put to death.

sentences.zh: 以平章政事完顏匡為尚書令。

translations.literal: Participation Councillor Wanyan Kuang was made Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Participation Councillor Wanyan Kuang was appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 五月，高麗賀即位。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Goryeo congratulated him on his enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Goryeo sent congratulations on his enthronement.

sentences.zh: 試宏詞科。

translations.literal: The Hongci examination was held.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongci examination was held.

sentences.zh: 七月，幸海王莊，臨奠魯國公主。

translations.literal: Seventh month: he visited Haiwang Manor and mourned the Princess of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he went to Haiwang Manor and mourned the Princess of Lu.

sentences.zh: 八月，萬秋節，宋遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Heavenly Longevity Festival: Song sent envoys with congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the Heavenly Longevity Festival, Song sent congratulatory envoys.

sentences.zh: 九月，如大房山，謁奠睿陵、裕陵、道陵。

translations.literal: Ninth month: he went to Great Fang Mountain and offered at Ruiling, Yuling, and Daoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he went to Great Fang Mountain and offered at Ruiling, Yuling, and Daoling.

sentences.zh: 百官表請建儲，不允。

translations.literal: The hundred officials memorialized begging that an heir be established; not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials begged that a crown prince be named; he refused.

sentences.zh: 十月，歲星犯左執法。

translations.literal: Tenth month: the Year Star invaded Left Law Enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Jupiter invaded the Left Law Enforcer asterism.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔戒勵風俗。

translations.literal: On jimao an edict admonished and encouraged customs.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao he issued an edict admonishing and encouraging public morals.

sentences.zh: 十一月，平陽地震，有聲如雷，自西北來。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Pingyang suffered an earthquake; a sound like thunder came from the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Pingyang was struck by an earthquake; a sound like thunder rolled in from the northwest.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔平陽地震，人戶三人死者免租稅一年，二人及傷者免一年，貧民死者給葬錢五千，傷者三千。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, an edict on the Pingyang earthquake: households with three dead were exempt from rent and tax for one year; those with two dead or with wounded were exempt for one year; poor dead were given five thousand in burial money and the wounded three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month an edict on the Pingyang earthquake granted one year’s rent and tax exemption to households with three dead, the same to those with two dead or wounded, five thousand cash for burying the poor dead, and three thousand for the wounded.

sentences.zh: 尚書令申王完顏匡薨。

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing, Prince Shen Wanyan Kuang, died.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Masters of Writing Prince Shen Wanyan Kuang died.

sentences.zh: 右丞相僕散端為左丞相，進封兄郢王永功為譙王，御史大夫張行簡為太保。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Pusan Duan became left chancellor; his elder brother, Prince Yong of Ying Yong Gong, was advanced to Prince of Qiao; and Censor-in-Chief Zhang Xingjian was made grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Pusan Duan became left chancellor; his elder brother Prince Yong of Ying, Yong Gong, was advanced to Prince of Qiao; and Censor-in-Chief Zhang Xingjian was made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 二年正月庚戌朔，日中有流星出，大如盆，其色碧，向西行，漸如車輪，尾長數丈，沒於濁中，至地複起，光散如火。

translations.literal: Year two, first month, new moon on gengxu: within the sun a meteor appeared, as large as a basin, blue-green in color, traveling west; gradually it became like a wheel, its tail several zhang long; it sank in murky air, reached the ground and rose again, and its light scattered like fire.
translations.idiomatic: In year two, on the gengxu new moon of the first month, a meteor burst from within the sun, basin-sized and blue-green, moving west; it swelled to wheel size with a tail many zhang long, sank into murk, struck the ground and rose again, and its light scattered like flame.

sentences.zh: 二月，客星入紫微垣，光散為赤龍。

translations.literal: Second month: a guest star entered the Purple Forbidden Enclosure; its light scattered into a red dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month a guest star entered the Purple Forbidden Enclosure; its light scattered into the shape of a red dragon.

sentences.zh: 地大震，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: A great earthquake occurred; the sound was like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: A great earthquake struck; the sound was like thunder.

sentences.zh: 以禮部侍郎耿端義為參知政事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Geng Duanyi was made participation councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Geng Duanyi was appointed participation councillor.

sentences.zh: 四月，校《大金儀禮》。

translations.literal: Fourth month: the Rites of Great Jin was collated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the court collated the Rites of Great Jin.

sentences.zh: 北方有黑氣，如大道，東西亙天。

translations.literal: In the north black qi lay like a great road spanning east and west across the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the north black vapor lay like a great road stretching east and west across the heavens.

sentences.zh: 徐、邳州河清五百餘里，以告宗廟社稷。

translations.literal: The rivers of Xu and Pi prefectures ran clear for more than five hundred li; the court reported this to the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The rivers of Xu and Pi prefectures ran clear for more than five hundred li; the court reported it to the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔儒臣編《續資治通鑒》。

translations.literal: Fifth month: an edict ordered Confucian officials to compile the Continuation of the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he ordered Confucian officials to compile the Continuation of the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 六月，大旱。

translations.literal: Sixth month: great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month a great drought struck.

sentences.zh: 下詔罪已，振貧民闕食者。

translations.literal: An edict of self-reproach was issued, and poor people lacking food were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict blaming himself and gave relief to poor people without food.

sentences.zh: 曲赦西京、太原兩路雜犯，死罪減一等，徒以下免。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty was granted for miscellaneous crimes in the Western Capital and Taiyuan circuits: death sentences were reduced one grade, and penal servitude and below were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty covered miscellaneous crimes in the Western Capital and Taiyuan circuits: death sentences were reduced one grade, and penal servitude and lesser punishments were waived.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，地震。

translations.literal: On bingyin there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin there was an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 七月，地震。

translations.literal: Seventh month: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month there was an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 八月，地震。

translations.literal: Eighth month: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month there was another earthquake.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，立子胙王從恪為皇太子。

translations.literal: On yichou his son Prince Zuo Congke was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou his son Prince Zuo Congke was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 萬秋節，宋遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Heavenly Longevity Festival: Song sent envoys with congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the Heavenly Longevity Festival Song sent congratulatory envoys.

sentences.zh: 獵於近郊。

translations.literal: He hunted in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 夏人侵葭州。

translations.literal: Western Xia invaded Jia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia invaded Jia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九月，地大震。

translations.literal: Ninth month: great earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month there was a great earthquake.

sentences.zh: 乙未，詔求直言，招勇敢，撫流亡。

translations.literal: On weimo an edict sought blunt counsel, recruited the bold, and comforted the displaced.
translations.idiomatic: On weimo he sought blunt counsel, recruited the bold, and comforted refugees.

sentences.zh: 庚子，遣使慰撫宣德行省軍士。

translations.literal: On gengzi he sent envoys to comfort the troops of the Xuande Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he sent envoys to comfort the troops of the Xuande Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 丙午，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: On bingwu the capital was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the capital was placed under martial alert.

sentences.zh: 上日出巡撫，百官請視朝，不允。

translations.literal: The emperor went out daily on inspection tours; the hundred officials begged that he hold court; not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He went out daily on inspection tours; the hundred officials begged him to hold court, and he refused.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，宣德行省罷。

translations.literal: On xinhai the Xuande Pacification Commission was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the Xuande Pacification Commission was abolished.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔撫諭中都、西京、清、滄被兵民戶。

translations.literal: On guichou an edict comforted war-affected households in the Central Capital, Western Capital, Qing, and Cang.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou an edict comforted households harmed by war in the Central Capital, Western Capital, Qing, and Cang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，獵於近郊。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: he hunted in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he hunted in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 中都大悲閣東渠內火自出，逾旬乃滅。

translations.literal: In the Central Capital, fire issued by itself inside the eastern canal at Great Compassion Pavilion; after more than ten days it died out.
translations.idiomatic: At the Central Capital, fire burst by itself inside the eastern canal at Great Compassion Pavilion and burned for more than ten days before dying out.

sentences.zh: 閣南殺竿下石罅中火自出，人近之即滅，俄複出，如是者複旬日。

translations.literal: South of the pavilion, fire issued from a stone crevice beneath the execution pole; when people drew near it died out, then soon reappeared, and so it continued for another ten days.
translations.idiomatic: South of the pavilion fire burst from a stone crevice under the execution pole; when anyone approached it went out, then flared up again, and this went on for another ten days.

sentences.zh: 中都火焮民居。

translations.literal: In the Central Capital fire burned common dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: In the Central Capital fire burned commoners’ houses.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, new moon on yimao: eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the yimao new moon, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 是歲大饑。

translations.literal: That year there was great famine.
translations.idiomatic: That year there was great famine.

sentences.zh: 禁百姓不得傳說邊事。

translations.literal: Common people were forbidden to spread rumors about frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were forbidden to spread rumors about frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年正月乙酉朔，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Year three, first month, new moon on yiyou: Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys with congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, on the yiyou new moon of the first month, envoys from Song, Goryeo, and Xia came with congratulations.

sentences.zh: 熒惑入氐中。

translations.literal: Mars entered the Di asterism.
translations.idiomatic: Mars entered the Di asterism.

sentences.zh: 二月，熒惑犯房宿。

translations.literal: Second month: Mars trespassed against the Fang mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Mars trespassed against the Fang mansion.

sentences.zh: 有大風從北來，髮屋折木，通玄門重關折，東華門重關折。

translations.literal: A great wind came from the north, tearing off roofs and snapping trees; the double gates of Tongxuan Gate broke, and the double gates of Donghua Gate broke.
translations.idiomatic: A great wind blew from the north, tearing off roofs and snapping trees; the inner and outer gates of Tongxuan Gate and of Donghua Gate were broken.

sentences.zh: 閏月，熒惑犯鍵閉星。

translations.literal: Intercalary month: Mars trespassed against the Key-Lock star.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Mars trespassed against the Key-Lock star.

sentences.zh: 三月，大悲閣災，延及民居。

translations.literal: Third month: the Dabei Pavilion burned, and the fire spread to common houses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Dabei Pavilion burned, and the blaze spread to private homes.

sentences.zh: 有黑氣起北方，廣長若大堤，內有三白氣貫之，如龍虎狀。

translations.literal: Black qi rose in the north, broad and long like a great dike; within it three white streams pierced through, shaped like dragons and tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Black vapor rose in the north, as broad and long as a great embankment, with three white streams running through it in the shape of dragons and tigers.

sentences.zh: 括民間馬，令職官出馬有差。

translations.literal: Horses were requisitioned among the people, and officials were ordered to furnish horses in fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: The court requisitioned horses from the populace and ordered officials to supply horses according to rank.

sentences.zh: 四月，我大元太祖法天啟運驛武皇帝來征。

translations.literal: Fourth month: our Great Yuan Founder, the emperor titled Align-with-Heaven, Opener-of-Fortune, and Expedited Martial, came on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month our Great Yuan Founder, Genghis Khan, titled Align-with-Heaven, Opener-of-Fortune, and Expedited Martial, marched to attack.

sentences.zh: 遣西北路招討使粘合合打乞和。

translations.literal: The Northwestern Route pacification commissioner Nianhe Heda was sent to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern Route pacification commissioner Nianhe Heda was dispatched to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 平章政事獨吉千家奴，參知政事胡沙行省事備邊。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Shuji Qianjiani and Participation Councillor Husha took charge of the branch secretariat to prepare the border.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Shuji Qianjiani and Participation Councillor Husha were put in charge of the branch secretariat to ready the frontier.

sentences.zh: 西京留守紇石烈胡沙虎行樞密院事。

translations.literal: Western Capital defender Hesheli Hushahu acted as Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Western Capital defender Hesheli Hushahu served as Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 參知事奧屯忠孝為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Participation Councillor Aotun Zhongxiao was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Participation Councillor Aotun Zhongxiao was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書梁𤨠為參知政事。

translations.literal: Ministry of Revenue Director Liang Ce was made Participation Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Revenue Director Liang Ce was appointed Participation Councillor.

sentences.zh: 六月壬寅，更定軍前賞罰格。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on renyin: the scale of rewards and penalties before the army was revised.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renyin, the rules for rewards and penalties on campaign were revised.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔獎諭行省官，慰撫軍士。

translations.literal: Eighth month: an edict praised and instructed the branch secretariat officials and comforted the troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict praised the branch secretariat officials and ordered the troops comforted.

sentences.zh: 千家奴、胡沙自撫州退軍，駐于宣平。

translations.literal: Qianjiani and Husha withdrew from Fuzhou and encamped at Xuanping.
translations.idiomatic: Qianjiani and Husha pulled back from Fuzhou and encamped at Xuanping.

sentences.zh: 河南大名路軍逃歸，下詔招撫之。

translations.literal: Troops of the Henan Daming circuit fled home; an edict was issued to win them back.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers of the Henan Daming circuit deserted home; the court issued an edict to win them back.

sentences.zh: 九月，千家奴、胡沙敗績於會河堡，居庸關失守。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Qianjiani and Husha were defeated at Huihe Fort, and Juyong Pass was lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Qianjiani and Husha were routed at Huihe Fort, and Juyong Pass fell.

sentences.zh: 禁男子不得輒出中都城門。

translations.literal: Men were forbidden to leave the Central Capital gates without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Men were forbidden to leave the Central Capital gates at will.

sentences.zh: 大元前軍至中至都，中都戒嚴。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan vanguard reached Zhongzhi Capital; the Central Capital was placed under martial law.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Yuan vanguard reached the capital region; the Central Capital was placed under martial law.

sentences.zh: 參知政事梁𤨠鎮撫京城。

translations.literal: Participation Councillor Liang Ce pacified the capital city.
translations.idiomatic: Participation Councillor Liang Ce was charged with pacifying the capital.

sentences.zh: 十月，每夜初更正，東、西北天明如月初出，經月乃滅。

translations.literal: Tenth month: at the first watch each night, the eastern and northwestern sky brightened like the moon at its first appearance, and only after a month did it fade.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, at the first watch each night the eastern and northwestern sky glowed like a new moon and did not fade for a month.

sentences.zh: 熒惑犯壘壁陣。

translations.literal: Mars trespassed against the Rampart formation.
translations.idiomatic: Mars trespassed against the Rampart formation.

sentences.zh: 上京留守徒單鎰遣同知烏古孫兀屯將兵二萬衛中都。

translations.literal: Shangjing defender Tudan Yi sent Vice Commissioner Wugusun Wutun with twenty thousand troops to guard the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjing defender Tudan Yi sent Vice Commissioner Wugusun Wutun with twenty thousand men to defend the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 泰州刺史朮虎高琪屯通玄門外。

translations.literal: Taizhou prefect Zhuhu Gaoqi encamped outside Tongxuan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou prefect Zhuhu Gaoqi encamped outside Tongxuan Gate.

sentences.zh: 上巡撫諸軍。

translations.literal: The emperor personally inspected the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally inspected the armies.

sentences.zh: 罷宣德行省。

translations.literal: The Xuande branch secretariat was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande branch secretariat was abolished.

sentences.zh: 十一月，殺河南陳言人郝贊。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Hao Zan of Henan, who had offered remonstrance, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Hao Zan of Henan, who had submitted remonstrance, was executed.

sentences.zh: 以上京留守徒單鎰為右丞相。

translations.literal: Shangjing defender Tudan Yi was made Right Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjing defender Tudan Yi was appointed Right Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 簽中都在城軍。

translations.literal: Troops in the capital city were mustered by roster.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison troops in the capital were mustered by roster.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈胡沙虎棄西京，走還京師，即以為右副元帥，權尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Hesheli Hushahu abandoned the Western Capital, fled back to the capital, and was thereupon made Right Vice Marshal and Acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Hesheli Hushahu abandoned the Western Capital and fled back to the capital, where he was made Right Vice Marshal and Acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時，德興府、弘州、昌平、懷來、縉山、豐潤、密雲、撫甯、集寧，東過平、灤，南至清、滄，由臨潢過遼河，西南至忻、代，皆歸大元。

translations.literal: At this time Dexing prefecture, Hongzhou, Changping, Huailai, Jinshan, Fengrun, Miyun, Funing, Jining, east through Ping and Luan, south to Qing and Cang, from Linhuang across the Liao River, and southwest to Xin and Dai—all submitted to the Great Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Dexing, Hongzhou, Changping, Huailai, Jinshan, Fengrun, Miyun, Funing, Jining, lands east to Ping and Luan, south to Qing and Cang, from Linhuang across the Liao River, and southwest to Xin and Dai had all gone over to the Great Yuan.

sentences.zh: 初，徒單鎰請徒桓、昌、撫百姓入內地。

translations.literal: Earlier Tudan Yi had asked to move the people of Huan, Chang, and Fu into the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tudan Yi had asked to relocate the people of Huan, Chang, and Fu into the interior.

sentences.zh: 上信梁𤨠議，以責鎰曰：「是自蹙境土也。

translations.literal: The emperor trusted Liang Ce’s advice and rebuked Yi, saying: “This is to cramp our own territory.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted Liang Ce’s view and rebuked Yi, saying, “That would only shrink our own territory.”

sentences.zh: 」及大元已定三州，上悔之。

translations.literal: After the Great Yuan had secured the three prefectures, the emperor regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Great Yuan had taken the three prefectures, the emperor regretted it.

sentences.zh: 至是，鎰複請置行省事于東京，備不虞。

translations.literal: Now Yi again asked to set up a branch secretariat at Dongjing to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Yi again asked to establish a branch secretariat at Dongjing against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 上不悅曰：「無故遣大臣，動搖人心。

translations.literal: The emperor, displeased, said: “To send a chief minister for no reason shakes the people’s hearts.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, displeased, said, “Sending a chief minister for no reason will shake the people’s hearts.”

sentences.zh: 」未幾，東京不守，上乃大悔。

translations.literal: Before long Dongjing could not be held, and the emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dongjing fell, and the emperor was filled with regret.

sentences.zh: 右副元帥胡沙虎請兵二萬屯宣德，詔與三千人屯媯川。

translations.literal: Right Vice Marshal Hushahu asked for twenty thousand troops to encamp at Xuande; the edict gave him three thousand to encamp at Guichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Marshal Hushahu asked for twenty thousand men at Xuande; the court allowed only three thousand at Guichuan.

sentences.zh: 平章政事千家奴、參知政事胡沙坐覆全軍，千家奴除名，胡沙責授咸平路兵馬總管。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Qianjiani and Participation Councillor Husha were punished for destroying the whole army; Qianjiani was struck from the rolls, and Husha was demoted to Xianping circuit military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Qianjiani and Participation Councillor Husha were punished for the annihilation of their army; Qianjiani was struck from office, and Husha was demoted to Xianping circuit military commander.

sentences.zh: 萬戶𠇗頭屯古北口。

translations.literal: Wanhu Guatou encamped at Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: Wanhu Guatou encamped at Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，簽陝西兩路漢軍五千人赴中都。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: five thousand Han troops of the two Shaanxi circuits were drafted to go to the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month five thousand Han soldiers from the two Shaanxi circuits were drafted for the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 太保張行簡、左丞相僕散端宿禁中議軍事。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Zhang Xingjian and Left Grand Councilor Pusan Duan lodged in the palace to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Zhang Xingjian and Left Grand Councilor Pusan Duan stayed in the palace to discuss military affairs.

sentences.zh: 左丞相僕散端罷。

translations.literal: Left Grand Councilor Pusan Duan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Left Grand Councilor Pusan Duan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 七月，有風自東來，吹帛一段，高數十丈，飛動如龍形，墜於拱辰門。

translations.literal: Seventh month: a wind came from the east and blew a length of silk, tens of zhang high, moving in flight like a dragon; it fell at Gongchen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an easterly wind lifted a bolt of silk tens of zhang high, swirling like a dragon, and cast it down at Gongchen Gate.

sentences.zh: 八月，萬秋節，以兵事不設宴。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Wanqiu Festival: because of the war no banquet was held.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on Wanqiu Festival, no banquet was held because of the fighting.

sentences.zh: 十月，曲赦西京、遼東、北京。

translations.literal: Tenth month: a partial amnesty was granted for the Western Capital, Liaodong, and Northern Capital circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month a partial amnesty was granted for the Western Capital, Liaodong, and Northern Capital circuits.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賑河東南路、南京路、陝西東路、山東西路、衛州旱災。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: relief was given for drought in Hedong South circuit, Nanjing circuit, Shaanxi East circuit, Shandong West circuit, and Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month drought relief was ordered for Hedong South, Nanjing, Shaanxi East, and Shandong West circuits and Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，夏國王李遵頊謝封冊。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Xia king Li Zunxu thanked the court for his investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xia king Li Zunxu thanked the court for his investiture.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年正月，賑河東陝西饑。

translations.literal: Zhi’ning year 1, first month: famine relief was given in Hedong and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhi’ning year 1, famine relief was ordered for Hedong and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二月，詔撫諭遼東。

translations.literal: Second month, an edict comforted and instructed Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month an edict went out to comfort and reassure Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 知大名府事烏古論誼謀不軌，伏誅。

translations.literal: Wugulun Yi, who governed Daming prefecture, plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Yi, administrator of Daming, plotted treason and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 三月，太陰、太白與日並見，相去尺餘。

translations.literal: Third month, the moon and Venus appeared together with the sun, a foot or so apart.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the moon and Venus stood with the sun at once, barely a foot apart.

sentences.zh: 五月，改元。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the court changed the reign era.

sentences.zh: 詔諭咸平路契丹部人之嘯聚者。

translations.literal: An edict admonished Khitan clansmen of Xianping Circuit who had gathered in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: An edict addressed the Khitan bands of Xianping Circuit who had risen in disorder.

sentences.zh: 起胡沙虎複為右副元帥，領武衛軍三千人屯通玄門外。

translations.literal: Hushahu was restored as right deputy grand marshal and led three thousand Martial Guard troops to camp outside Tongxuan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hushahu was recalled as right deputy grand marshal and stationed three thousand Martial Guard troops outside Tongxuan Gate.

sentences.zh: 陝西大旱。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered a great drought.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi was stricken with severe drought.

sentences.zh: 六月，夏人犯保安州，殺刺史，犯慶陽府，殺同知府事。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Xia forces attacked Bao'an prefecture and killed the prefect; they attacked Qingyang prefecture and killed the associate prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Xia troops raided Bao'an, killed the prefect, then struck Qingyang and killed the associate prefect.

sentences.zh: 以戶部尚書胥鼎、刑部尚書王維翰為參知政事。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Xu Ding and Minister of Justice Wang Weihan were made participation councillors.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ding, minister of revenue, and Wang Weihan, minister of justice, were appointed participation councillors.

sentences.zh: 八月，尚書左丞完顏元奴將兵備邊。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wanyan Yuannu led troops to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Left Vice Director Wanyan Yuannu took the field to ready the border defenses.

sentences.zh: 詔軍官、軍士賜賚有差。

translations.literal: An edict granted officers and soldiers rewards in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered graded rewards for officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 大霧，晝晦。

translations.literal: Heavy fog fell; daylight turned dim.
translations.idiomatic: A heavy fog blanketed the capital until broad day seemed twilight.

sentences.zh: 治中福海別將兵屯城北。

translations.literal: Administration Vice-Director Fu Hai separately led troops to camp north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Administration Vice-Director Fu Hai posted a separate force north of the city.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，胡沙虎矯詔以誅反者，招福海執而殺之，奪其兵。

translations.literal: On xinmao Hushahu forged an edict to execute rebels, summoned Fu Hai, seized and killed him, and took his troops.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Hushahu forged an edict against traitors, lured Fu Hai in, killed him, and seized his command.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，自通玄門入，殺知大興府徒單南平、刑部會郎徒單沒拈于廣陽門西。

translations.literal: On renchen he entered through Tongxuan Gate and killed Daxing prefect Tushan Nanping and Ministry of Justice vice minister Tushan Monian west of Guangyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he entered by Tongxuan Gate and slew Daxing Prefect Tushan Nanping and Ministry of Justice Vice Minister Tushan Monian west of Guangyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 福海男符寶鄯陽、都統石古乃率眾拒戰，死之。

translations.literal: Fu Hai's son Fubao Shanyang and commandant-in-chief Shigu Nai led men to resist and were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hai's son Fubao Shanyang and Commandant-in-Chief Shigu Nai rallied troops to fight back and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎叩東華門，遣人呼守直親軍百戶冬兒、五十戶蒲察六斤，不應。

translations.literal: Hushahu knocked at Donghua Gate and sent men to summon the direct-guard centurion Dong'er and fifty-household chief Pucha Liujin; they did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Hushahu battered Donghua Gate and sent for the direct-guard centurion Dong'er and fifty-household chief Pucha Liujin; neither would answer.

sentences.zh: 許以世襲猛安三品官職，亦不應。

translations.literal: He promised hereditary meng'an status and third-rank posts; still they would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He offered hereditary meng'an standing and third-rank offices, yet they still refused.

sentences.zh: 都點檢徒單渭河縋而出，護衛斜烈掊鎖啟門，胡沙虎以兵入宮，盡遂衛士，代以其黨，自稱監國都元帥。

translations.literal: Chief Inspector Tushan Weihe let himself down by rope and fled; guard Xielie battered the lock open; Hushahu entered the palace with troops, drove out all the guards, replaced them with his own men, and styled himself Regent Grand Marshal of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Inspector Tushan Weihe was lowered by rope and escaped; guard Xielie smashed the lock and opened the gate. Hushahu entered the palace with soldiers, expelled the guards, filled their posts with his own men, and proclaimed himself regent grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，逼上出宮。

translations.literal: On guisi he forced the emperor from the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he drove the emperor from the palace.

sentences.zh: 以素車載至故邸，以武衛軍二百人錮守之。

translations.literal: He had him carried in an unadorned carriage to his former residence and confined him with two hundred Martial Guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: He placed him in a plain carriage, sent him to his old residence, and held him under guard with two hundred Martial Guard troops.

sentences.zh: 尚宮左夫人鄭氏為內職，掌寶璽，聞難，端居璽所待變。

translations.literal: Inner Palace Left Lady Zheng held the office of inner service and kept the imperial seals; hearing of the crisis, she sat upright in the seal chamber awaiting events.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Palace Left Lady Zheng, keeper of the imperial seals, heard of the upheaval and sat unmoving in the seal chamber, waiting for whatever came.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎遣黃門入收璽，鄭曰：「璽，天子所用，胡沙虎人臣，取將何為？

translations.literal: Hushahu sent a eunuch to take the seals; Zheng said: "The seal is what the Son of Heaven uses — Hushahu is a subject; what will he do by taking it?
translations.idiomatic: Hushahu sent a eunuch to seize the seals. Lady Zheng said, "The seal belongs to the Son of Heaven. Hushahu is only a subject — what use has he for it?

sentences.zh: 」黃門曰：「今天時大變，主上猶且不保，況璽乎？

translations.literal: " The eunuch said: "Heaven and earth have greatly changed; even His Majesty cannot be preserved — how much less the seal?
translations.idiomatic: " The eunuch said, "The times have overturned; even the emperor may not survive — how much less a seal?

sentences.zh: 御侍當思自脫計。

translations.literal: A lady attendant should think of a way to save herself."
translations.idiomatic: You who serve in the palace should think first of saving yourself."

sentences.zh: 」鄭厲聲罵曰：「若輩宮中近侍，恩遇尤隆，君難不以死報之，反為逆豎奪璽耶！

translations.literal: " Zheng shouted curses: "You palace attendants have enjoyed the greatest favor — at your lord's crisis you do not repay with death, yet instead help a rebel seize the seal!
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Zheng cried out in fury, "You who wait on the emperor have been favored beyond measure. When your lord is in peril you do not die for him, yet you would hand the seal to a traitor!

sentences.zh: 我死可必，璽必不與。

translations.literal: My death is certain, but I will never give up the seal."
translations.idiomatic: I shall surely die, but I will never surrender the seal."

sentences.zh: 」遂瞑目不語。

translations.literal: " She closed her eyes and would not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " She shut her eyes and would not speak again.

sentences.zh: 黃門出，胡沙虎卒取「宣命之寶」，偽除其黨醜奴為德州防禦使、烏古論奪剌順天軍節度使、提控宿直將軍徒單金壽永定軍節度使，及其餘黨凡數十人，皆遷宮。

translations.literal: The eunuch withdrew; Hushahu finally took the "Seal of Imperial Commands" and falsely appointed his follower Chounu defense commissioner of Dezhou, Wugulun Duola Shuntian Army military commissioner, Detached Control Commissioner of the Direct Guard Tushan Jinshou Yongding Army military commissioner, and several dozen other partisans — all moved into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch left, Hushahu seized the Seal of Imperial Commands and forged appointments: Chounu as defense commissioner of Dezhou, Wugulun Duola as Shuntian Army military commissioner, Tushan Jinshou of the Direct Guard as Yongding Army military commissioner, and several dozen more of his faction, all quartered in the palace.

sentences.zh: 遂使宦者李思中害上于邸。

translations.literal: He then had the eunuch Li Sizhong murder the emperor at the residence.
translations.idiomatic: He then had the eunuch Li Sizhong kill the emperor at the residence.

sentences.zh: 誘奉御和尚作書急召其父左丞元奴議事，元奴以軍來，並其子皆殺之。

translations.literal: He tricked Attendant-in-Ordinary Heshang into writing to urgently summon his father Vice Director Yuannu to discuss affairs; Yuannu came with troops and he killed both father and son.
translations.idiomatic: He induced Attendant-in-Ordinary Heshang to write an urgent summons to his father, Vice Director Yuannu. When Yuannu marched in with troops, Hushahu killed father and son together.

sentences.zh: 十月辛亥，元帥右監軍朮虎高琪殺胡沙虎於其第。

translations.literal: Tenth month, xinhai, Right Army Supervisor of the Marshalate Tuhu Gaoqi killed Hushahu at his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on xinhai, Marshalate Right Army Supervisor Tuhu Gaoqi slew Hushahu in his own house.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎者，紇石烈執中也。

translations.literal: Hushahu was Heshilie Zhizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Hushahu was none other than Heshilie Zhizhong.

sentences.zh: 宣宗乃下詔削其官爵。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor then issued an edict stripping his ranks and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong then issued an edict stripping him of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 贈石古乃順州刺史，鄯陽順天軍節度副使，凡從二人拒戰者，千戶賞錢五百貫，謀克三百貫，蒲輦散軍二百貫，各遷官兩階，戰沒者贈賞付其家。

translations.literal: Shigu Nai was posthumously made prefect of Shunzhou; Shanyang associate military commissioner of Shuntian Army; for all who followed the two in resistance, thousand-households were given five hundred strings of cash, company commanders three hundred, infantry soldiers two hundred, each promoted two ranks; those who died in battle — posthumous rewards were paid to their families.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu Nai was posthumously made prefect of Shunzhou; Shanyang, associate military commissioner of the Shuntian Army. Those who had fought with them were rewarded by rank: thousand-households five hundred strings of cash, company commanders three hundred, common soldiers two hundred, each raised two grades; the families of the slain received posthumous grants.

sentences.zh: 冬兒加龍虎衛上將軍，再遷宿進將軍。

translations.literal: Dong'er was made General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and again promoted to Bivouac Advance General.
translations.idiomatic: Dong'er was made general-in-chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and soon after promoted to bivouac advance general.

sentences.zh: 蒲察六斤加定遠大將軍、武衛軍鈐轄。

translations.literal: Pucha Liujin was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and commandant of the Martial Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Liujin was made general who pacifies the distance and commandant of the Martial Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 石古乃子尚幼，給俸八貫石，敕有司，俟其年十五以聞。

translations.literal: Shigu Nai's son was still young; an eight-picul stipend was granted and the relevant offices ordered to report when he reached fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu Nai's son was still a child; the court granted an eight-picul stipend and ordered the offices to report when he turned fifteen.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年，詔追複衛王諡曰紹。

translations.literal: In Zhenyou year four, an edict restored Prince Wei's posthumous title as Shao.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou year four an edict restored Prince Wei's posthumous title to Shao.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：衛紹王政亂於內，兵敗於外，其滅亡已有徵矣。

translations.literal: Appraisal: Prince Wei Shaowang's government was chaotic within and his armies defeated without — the signs of extinction were already plain.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Within, Prince Wei Shaowang's rule was in disorder; without, his armies were broken — the omens of ruin were already clear.

sentences.zh: 身弑國蹙，記注亡失，南遷後不復紀載。

translations.literal: The ruler was assassinated and the state compressed; court records were lost, and after the southward move they were no longer kept.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign was murdered and the realm shrank; the annals were lost, and after the court moved south they were no longer maintained.

sentences.zh: 皇朝中統三年，翰林學士承旨王鶚有志論著，求大安、崇慶事不可得，采摭當時詔令，故金部令史竇祥年八十九，耳目聰明，能記憶舊事，從之得二十餘條。

translations.literal: In our dynasty's Zhongtong year three, Hanlin Academician Wang He, as chief compiler, wished to write a history; he could not obtain matters from Da'an and Chongqing, but collected edicts of the time; the former Jin Ministry of Revenue clerk Dou Xiang, eighty-nine years old, clear in sight and hearing and able to remember old events — from him he got more than twenty items.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong year three of our dynasty, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Wang He set out to write the history but could not recover events from the Da'an and Chongqing reigns. He gathered edicts of the day and turned to Dou Xiang, a former Jin Ministry of Revenue clerk of eighty-nine, still keen of eye and ear and able to recall old affairs — from him he obtained a little more than twenty entries.

sentences.zh: 司天提點張正之寫災異十六條，張承旨家手本載舊事五條，金禮部尚書楊雲翼日錄四十條，陳老日錄三十條，藏在史館。

translations.literal: Astronomy Commissioner Zhang Zhengzhi copied sixteen entries on calamities; five old affairs recorded in a hand copy at Academician Zhang's home; forty daily entries by former Jin Minister of Rites Yang Yunyi; thirty daily entries by Old Chen — all stored in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy Commissioner Zhang Zhengzhi transcribed sixteen records of portents; a household manuscript at Academician Zhang's home preserved five old items; former Jin Minister of Rites Yang Yunyi left forty daily notes and Old Chen thirty — all kept in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 條件雖多，重復者三之二。

translations.literal: Though the items were many, two-thirds were duplicates.
translations.idiomatic: For all their number, two-thirds repeated one another.

sentences.zh: 惟所載李妃、完顏匡定策，獨吉千家奴兵敗，紇石烈執中作難，及日食、星變、地震、氛昆，不相背盭。

translations.literal: Only the entries on Consort Li, Wanyan Kuang's plotting, Tugu Qianjianu's defeat, Heshilie Zhizhong's revolt, and eclipses, stellar anomalies, earthquakes, and miasma did not contradict one another.
translations.idiomatic: Only the accounts of Consort Li, Wanyan Kuang's conspiracy, Tugu Qianjianu's defeat, Heshilie Zhizhong's coup, and the eclipses, strange stars, earthquakes, and uncanny vapors agreed without conflict.

sentences.zh: 今校其重出，刪其繁雜。

translations.literal: Now duplicates are collated and the redundant removed.
translations.idiomatic: Duplicates have now been compared and the clutter cut away.

sentences.zh: 《章宗實錄》詳其前事，《宜宗實錄》詳其後事。

translations.literal: The Veritable Record of Zhangzong details earlier matters; the Veritable Record of Xuanzong details later matters.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Record of Zhangzong treats the earlier reign; the Veritable Record of Xuanzong treats what followed.

sentences.zh: 又于金掌奏目女官大明居士王氏所紀，得資明夫人援璽一事，附著於篇，亦可以存其梗概云爾。

translations.literal: Also from the records of the Jin palace memorial registrar, Palace Woman Dame Bright Heaven Wang, the affair of Lady Ziming holding fast to the seal was obtained and appended in this chapter, so that its outline may yet be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: From the memorial register kept by the Jin palace woman Dame Bright Heaven Wang, the episode of Lady Ziming defending the seal was recovered and set down here, so that its outline might still survive.
